transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-14 08:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Rivera (Redwood SE), Akira Sato (Redwood Partnerships), Nina Patel (Redwood Solutions), Lena Park (Catalyst Head of Platform), Tomás Reyes (Catalyst VP Sales), Amira Hassan (Catalyst Security Lead), Eric Lowe (Catalyst Solutions Architect), Jules Carter (Catalyst Partner Ops)

Summary:
Quick partner cadence to triage top Catalyst opportunities, align on pilot scope, and unblock compliance review. Focus: which deals to co-orient, what benchmarks to run, and next steps for a pilot.

Topics: co-sell routing, pilot metrics, security artifacts, joint enablement, timeline and stakeholders.

00:00:12 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, happy Valentine's day by the way, um, quick roll call, and then we wanted to run through a proposed cadence for co-selling with Catalyst and call out the top two deals we think are ripe for acceleration.
00:00:28 - Lena Park: Hi, yeah thanks. Lena here. Good to see you all.
00:00:31 - Tomás Reyes: Tomás on for sales. Morning.
00:00:34 - Diego Rivera: Diego, SE, Redwood.
00:00:36 - Amira Hassan: Amira, security.
00:00:38 - Eric Lowe: Eric, solutions.
00:00:40 - Maya Chen: Cool, great. Quick agenda: one, align on deal prioritization; two, pilot scope and success metrics; three, security/compliance blockers; four, next steps. Does that work?
00:00:54 - Jules Carter: Works for me.
00:00:56 - Akira Sato: Yep.

00:01:10 - Maya Chen: Okay, Tomás do you want to start with the two target accounts you flagged last week and why you think they're ready for a co-sell push?
00:01:18 - Tomás Reyes: Sure. So the first is Northbridge Health — big EMR modernization push, they already have a PoC with one of our competitors but they're under cost pressure. The second is Meridian Retail — they're piloting recommendation inference and they like open model approach. Both are roughly mid-enterprise, and both have an exec sponsor we can engage with.
00:01:43 - Maya Chen: Got it. Any context on timeline on Northbridge?
00:01:45 - Tomás Reyes: They want production by end of Q2, so like a May rollout target, but security gating will be the slow lane there.
00:01:54 - Amira Hassan: That's likely true — for healthcare we need SOC2 plus some extra audit trail requirements, right? We'll need KMS integration and clear deletion policies.
00:02:05 - Diego Rivera: Quick clarifier, do we know if Northbridge requires on-prem or VPC private deployment? That will affect whether Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private is recommended.
00:02:15 - Lena Park: They said they prefer VPC, possibly a private deployment. They listed data residency concerns for PII.
00:02:22 - Maya Chen: Okay, so security is front-and-center. For Meridian Retail what's their main constraint?
00:02:28 - Tomás Reyes: Latency and cost. They run high QPS at peak shopping hours, they have a hard latency SLO for recommendations. They're price sensitive though so we can't default to premium dedicated unless we prove unit economics with batching.
00:02:42 - Diego Rivera: That's a classic latency vs cost tradeoff — we'll want to show batching and cache profiles, plus our quantization recommendations. I can sketch initial perf numbers in the architecture deep-dive.
00:02:53 - Eric Lowe: On the tech side, their current infra is Kubernetes in GCP, using managed GPUs through CloudEndpointX right now. We want to show Redwood's deployment model maps to their infra and migration path.
00:03:07 - Akira Sato: And on the partnerships side, we suggested a co-branded pilot offer — Redwood provides credits and a joint case study if they commit to a 3-month pilot.

00:03:22 - 00:03:46 (crosstalk)
00:03:22 - Lena Park: Quick question, what exactly is in the co-sell offer?
00:03:25 - Maya Chen: Right — short version, we'll provide a pilot package: up to X hours of compute credits on Dedicated or Hosted with a preferred pricing floor, plus an enablement bundle (architect time, runbooks, and a benchmark report). In return we ask for a joint reference and a short case study if things go well.
00:03:44 - Tomás Reyes: Sounds fair, but we need clarity on how leads are routed and revenue share.
00:03:49 - Akira Sato: We usually propose a referral credit plus joint-opportunity registration in CRM. We'll put a simple split on influenced revenue for the pilot conversion. I'll circulate a one-pager.

00:04:10 - Maya Chen: Great. Let's pivot to pilot metrics — Diego, can you run through what we'd measure and how to instrument?
00:04:16 - Diego Rivera: Yeah, so primary metrics: end-to-end latency p50/p95, tokens-per-second throughput, cost per 1M tokens, and quality metrics tied to their own eval sets (e.g., top-N click uplift for recommendations). We also want to measure cold-start LLM latency and KV cache hit rates. For Meridian, focus on p95 latency under peak qps; for Northbridge, focus on compliance and throughput for batched EHR requests.
00:04:44 - Lena Park: For Northbridge the success criteria will be: SOC2 artifacts validated, KMS integration tested, and a sub-second median latency for specific query shapes.
00:04:55 - Amira Hassan: Also retention controls — can you ensure logs are redactable and audit logs are exportable? We need to present to internal audit.
00:05:04 - Diego Rivera: Yes, we have audit log exports and can integrate with their SIEM. I'll include sample log formats in the docs.

00:05:20 - Maya Chen: On the tech blockers, Eric, are there any migration concerns if they move off CloudEndpointX?
00:05:25 - Eric Lowe: Main thing is model compatibility and custom tokenization. We've seen drift when switching runtimes. Also the KV cache semantics differ, so we'd want an initial bench to validate fidelity of outputs.
00:05:38 - Diego Rivera: We can run a side-by-side bench with the same prompts and seeds — Diego to own that test plan.
00:05:45 - Maya Chen: Perfect. Now security — Amira can you summarize must-haves?
00:05:50 - Amira Hassan: Sure. At minimum: SOC2 Type II report, encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS, SSO with SAML + provisioning, RBAC for team separation, and data residency controls. Also, we may need an option for on-prem air-gapped for HCLS later.
00:06:08 - Maya Chen: We're able to support SAML and RBAC; KMS support is documented but I'll share the integration notes. For SOC2 we have a summary and can provide auditor contact.
00:06:17 - Akira Sato: We'll include the security pack link in the follow-ups (redwood.com/security-pack link).

00:06:30 - 00:07:05 (longer pause while someone shares screen)
00:07:06 - Diego Rivera: Okay, I'm sharing an architecture sketch now — high level flows: client -> Catalyst API -> Redwood edge -> serving pool (dedicated or hosted) -> KMS for encryption. We'll show options for prefix caching and KV layer.
00:07:24 - Eric Lowe: On the slide, can you call out where we run inference for low latency? If we're in GCP, we want region alignment and possibly dedicated pools in us-central1.
00:07:36 - Diego Rivera: Yep, we'll recommend co-locating with their infra and provide region fallback policies.

00:07:50 - Maya Chen: I want to call attention to cost controls — Redwood Optimize can run a recommendation to pick quantization + batch size combos per workload. Diego, do we have a rough cost delta for Meridian's expected qps?
00:08:03 - Diego Rivera: Based on their estimate (about 200 rps peak for a 100ms target) we think using batching and int8 quant will reduce per-token cost by ~35% vs naive float32 on dedicated. But we need their exact sequence length distribution.
00:08:18 - Lena Park: We'll share that. We'll also need an estimate for egress, as some of our infra routes need careful accounting.
00:08:24 - Maya Chen: Good point — we'll include egress and request unit assumptions in the pricing snapshot.

00:08:35 - Tomás Reyes: I'd like to talk about co-sell motions — what's the handoff between Redwood AE and Catalyst reps? We're thinking joint exec sponsorship calls, but day-to-day who owns the opportunity in CRM?
00:08:47 - Akira Sato: For pilots we recommend Catalyst lead the opportunity with Redwood as a registered partner. We'll register influence and ensure lead crediting. Akira to send the partner registration workflow.
00:08:58 - Jules Carter: From ops, we need a simple SLAs doc for handoffs and expected response times during pilot.
00:09:05 - Maya Chen: We'll provide an SLA-ish pilot runbook: escalation contacts, expected triage times, and the benchmark timeline.

00:09:18 - 00:09:45 (interruption, brief audio glitch)
00:09:46 - Amira Hassan: Sorry, dropped for a sec, I'm back. On the compliance documents, can we get a redlined contract example for data handling? We want to pre-clear some clauses.
00:09:57 - Maya Chen: Yes, legal can share a template. I'll put that in the follow-up.

00:10:10 - Diego Rivera: Quick technical note: for the Northbridge EHR use case, we suggest a dedicated pool with strict RBAC and a private VPC connector to satisfy their data-in-transit requirements. We'll show how Redwood Private maps to that.
00:10:24 - Lena Park: That helps. Also, for auditing, we need retention policy options for logs — 90 days is the baseline but some audit groups want longer.
00:10:33 - Akira Sato: We can support configurable retention; we'll propose options in the security pack.

00:10:45 - Maya Chen: Moving into timing — suggested timeline: this week share docs, next week architecture deep-dive, week after start a 4-week pilot for Meridian and a separate compliance validation track for Northbridge. Does that sequencing make sense?
00:11:03 - Tomás Reyes: Yes, that sounds workable. For sales incentives, do we have any co-funding to accelerate procurement?
00:11:11 - Akira Sato: We can offer limited co-fund credits for the pilot if Catalyst brings a qualified lead and registers it. Details in the partner playbook.

00:11:25 - Maya Chen: Alright let's do a quick risk assessment for both deals — call out top 3 risks and mitigations.
00:11:32 - Diego Rivera: For Northbridge: 1) Compliance gating — mitigation: early audit pack and KMS integration; 2) Model fidelity drift — mitigation: side-by-side bench and regression evals; 3) Procurement timeline — mitigation: pre-shared contract template.
00:11:53 - Tomás Reyes: For Meridian: 1) Cost vs latency tradeoff — mitigation: Redwood Optimize recommendations and trial of batching; 2) Peak autoscaling surprises — mitigation: dedicated pool with burst capacity; 3) Integration effort — mitigation: shared runbook and CA template.

00:12:13 - Eric Lowe: On the benching plan, do we have synthetic workload generator or will Catalyst supply real anonymized prompts?
00:12:20 - Lena Park: We can anonymize and share a sample set, will check compliance but likely yes for Meridian; for Northbridge probably only synthetic with de-identification.
00:12:31 - Diego Rivera: Fine. We'll draft a bench plan that supports both synthetic and real prompt sets.

00:12:40 - Maya Chen: Alright, any competitor concerns — Tomás you mentioned CloudEndpointX — what posture do we take?
00:12:46 - Tomás Reyes: CloudEndpointX is quoting aggressively on price, their support model is lighter though. We should emphasize Redwood's reliability and observability, and the joint GTM angle with Catalyst.
00:12:58 - Akira Sato: We'll also highlight our Optimize toolkit and the transparent unit economics.

00:13:10 - 00:13:40 (longer discussion about joint event ideas and content)
00:13:41 - Jules Carter: We can do a webinar in late Q1, maybe pair a Catalyst customer success story with Redwood technical deep-dive. I'll draft dates and share.

00:14:05 - Maya Chen: Great. Quick check — who will own the pilot kickoff coordination?
00:14:10 - Jules Carter: I'll own scheduling on the Catalyst side, Maya if you can set internal Redwood contacts that will be the single thread.
00:14:17 - Maya Chen: Yep I'll be the Redwood single-thread and Diego will be the technical lead.

00:14:25 - 00:14:50 (summarizing)
00:14:26 - Maya Chen: To recap: Redwood to send co-sell playbook, pricing snapshot, security pack link and architecture checklist. Diego to prepare bench plan and initial sizing. Catalyst to share usage CSV and prompt samples where allowed. We'll set the architecture deep-dive for next Thursday, 60 minutes. Action items and owners are in the notes.
00:14:50 - Lena Park: Thanks all. One more ask: can you put the pilot success metrics in a one-page dashboard we can use to show execs?
00:14:57 - Diego Rivera: Absolutely, we'll produce a one-pager with p50/p95, cost per 1M tokens, cache hit, and business metric (click uplift).
00:15:06 - Maya Chen: Perfect. Any last minute items?
00:15:10 - Amira Hassan: Please make sure the KMS notes include key rotation policies — internal audit will ask.
00:15:16 - Maya Chen: We'll add that.

00:15:25 - 00:15:45 (closing logistics about calendar invites and files)
00:15:26 - Akira Sato: I'll post the co-sell one-pager to the shared drive and add Akira to the CRM opp.
00:15:33 - Maya Chen: Thanks. Maya to follow up with deck and files by EOD Friday. Diego to draft bench plan by Tuesday.

00:15:45 - 00:51:50 (some smaller side conversations, clarifications, and link-sharing)
00:51:51 - Maya Chen: Alright folks, thanks for the time. We'll circulate notes and action items. Talk soon.
00:51:58 - Lena Park: Thanks everyone.
00:52:00 - Meeting ends.

References and links mentioned: https://redwood.example.com/partner-playbook (co-sell one-pager), https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (SOC2/KMS notes), shared sheet: (Catalyst traffic profile spreadsheet) — link to be provided by customer.

Notes about transcript quality: automated transcription with some entity errors (CloudEndpointX sometimes transcribed as Cloud End Point), occasional dropped syllables, speaker labels are a mix of names and roles.
